subject: physics
question_text: What is the relation between the pressure and the internal energy of a gas?

mark_split.label: PV in terms of internal energy

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Very Short Answer Question 7 (printed p.137). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: PV = ⅔E, with E the total translational kinetic energy of the gas, follows from PV = ⅓Nmv̄² = ⅔N(½mv̄²); dividing through by V gives P = ⅔(E/V), matching NCERT Class-11 Chapter 13. This card answers for the gas's total internal energy E — the companion question about the average kinetic energy of one molecule is a separate card.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: PV in terms of internal energy
lines: For an ideal gas the internal energy
is purely kinetic. For a monoatomic
gas, it is entirely the translational
steps.margin_note: First mark. State that E is the total translational kinetic energy, then write PV = ⅔E.
steps.why: Kinetic theory gives PV = ⅓Nmv̄² = ⅔N(½mv̄²). The sum N(½mv̄²) over all the molecules is exactly the total translational kinetic energy E, so the same result reads PV = ⅔E.
common_mistakes: Writing PV = E, leaving out the two-thirds factor.
Treating E as the kinetic energy of one molecule instead of the total for the whole gas.

recall.must_convey: That PV equals two thirds E, where E is the total translational kinetic energy of the gas.
accept: E is the total kinetic energy
internal energy of the whole gas
reject: P equals two thirds n half m v squared

steps.memory_tip: E is the whole gas's energy. PV is two thirds of it.

steps.label: Pressure per unit volume
lines: The pressure is two-thirds of the
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Rearrange PV = ⅔E to P = ⅔(E/V) and name E/V as the energy per unit volume.
steps.why: Dividing PV = ⅔E through by V gives the pressure directly as a fraction of the energy density E/V — a way of reading the same relation that connects a bulk, measurable quantity, pressure, to the energy packed into each unit volume of gas.
common_mistakes: Writing P = ⅔E instead of P = ⅔(E/V) — the volume must be divided out.
Calling E/V the kinetic energy of one molecule. It is the total energy per unit volume.

recall.must_convey: That P equals two thirds of E by V, the translational kinetic energy per unit volume.
accept: P equals two thirds E by V
pressure is two thirds the energy density

steps.memory_tip: Divide both sides of PV = ⅔E by V to get pressure as energy per unit volume.

insider_note: This question asks for the gas's total internal energy E, not the energy of one molecule — keep E extensive throughout both steps.
